Awhile ago I made a post and in this post I mentioned an idea I had. I gave it the placeholder name Dreamification, which was stupid, but I simply hadn't come up with a name for it yet. Eventually I settled on Phantasmagoria. Phantasmagoria is,

Dictionary.com:

  1. a shifting series of phantasms, illusions, or deceptive appearances, as in a dream or as created by the imagination.
  2. a changing scene made up of many elements.
  3. an optical illusion produced by a magic lantern or the like in which figures increase or diminish in size, pass into each other, dissolve, etc.

Webster:

  1. an exhibition of optical effects and illusions
  2. a. a constantly shifting complex succession of things seen or imagined
    b. a scene that constantly changes
  3. a bizarre or fantastic combination, collection, or assemblage

Oxford:

  1. A sequence of real or imaginary images like that seen in a dream.

A word used to describe a dream-like phenomenon? Sounds like it was meant to be. A year later, I hit a new dilemma. I had a new idea, but I didn't have a name for it. Just today I revisited the word Phantasmagoria and checked out some synonyms. I then looked at the word Phantasm. A Phantasm is,

Dictionary.com:

  1. an apparition or specter.
  2. a creation of the imagination or fancy; fantasy.
  3. a mental image or representation of a real object.
  4. an illusory likeness of something.

Webster

  1. a product of fantasy: such as
    a. delusive appearance : illusion
    b. ghost, specter
    c. a figment of the imagination
  2. a mental representation of a real object

Oxford

literary
1. An illusion, apparition, or ghost.

archaic
1.1. An illusory likeness of something.

The common theme is illusory likeness, which is exactly what the original Dreamification/Phantasmagoria idea is. With that in mind, I concluded that Phantasm is a better word to describe that idea than Phantasmagoria and that Phantasmagoria will be the word to describe this new idea I had. Now that I've settled on a fitting name for this idea, I can begin the creation of the first one.
